clue.text: Draw deceased PM without husband

indicators.note: going without something means leaving it out, so one letter is dropped from the prime minister's name

explanation.surface: A grim tie: a dead prime minister, minus the man he never married.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from HEATH to leave HEAT. Edward Heath is the go-to crossword PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A race or contest where two competitors finish exactly level is a tie, the noun sense of draw.

clue.text: Endlessly creating names for waterproofing product

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to dub is to give a name to

explanation.surface: Endless brainstorming of brand names for a new waterproofer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dubbin is a greasy dressing rubbed into leather boots to keep water out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a wax and oil preparation applied to leather to soften and waterproof it.

clue.text: See 23
Difficult ship for one reluctant to compromise?

explanation.surface: An awkward vessel asks whether its captain is stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a 'hard liner' as a difficult ship is a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks rigidly to a policy or position and refuses concessions in negotiation.

clue.text: Meet a ship with man excited by drugs

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so they are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor on the quay, high on drugs, goes to meet a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphetamines are synthetic stimulant drugs, sometimes prescribed and often abused as speed.

clue.text: Insect swallowed by black American bird

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside whatever swallows it, so the insect sits within the other letters

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A black American bird gulps down a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Fear evident in the manner of soldier at sea

parts.note: French à la, in the style of
a Royal Marine, a soldier serving with the navy

explanation.surface: A soldier on a ship shows plain fright.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden anxious feeling of danger, a noun synonym for fear.

clue.text: Turn up, wearing tie, having a common plan

indicators.note: something worn is put on around the wearer, so the tie word goes round the first piece

parts.note: to tether is to tie up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Show up in a tie because everyone agreed on the dress code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive', but splits into a noun and a direction signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People acting together are united, sharing the same intention and acting in concert.

clue.text: Treat with pills a doctor swallowed

explanation.surface: A doctor gulped down a few tablets himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To medicate someone is to administer drugs to them as therapy.

clue.text: Bench for sport to exercise bust

parts.note: a bank is a row or bench, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: Gym equipment for a sport being used to work out the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' reads as a body part to exercise, but it is the informal adjective meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust is the informal way of saying a firm or person has failed financially and cannot pay debts.

clue.text: Artist returning without painting finally dropped

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the artist's name is read from the end
without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed name sits around the single letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas, French painter of ballet dancers

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word painting

explanation.surface: A painter came back having given up his art, and his spirits fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: SAGED is wrapped round the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagged and dropped both describe something sinking or drooping downwards under weight, a past-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: Cheats accepting punishment for nonsense

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the punishment goes inside the cheating word

parts.note: to fiddle is to cheat, as with accounts
to take stick is to be punished or criticised

explanation.surface: Swindlers who take their penalties call the charges rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Setter's wood for making model

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: The setter keeps some timber for making a model, as hobbyists do.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Setter's wood' as 'the setter has wood', I + DEAL. Deal is a crossword favourite for softwood planks.
explanation.definitionFit: A model as an adjective or noun is a perfect example to copy, which is exactly what an ideal is.

clue.text: Mysterious Houdini finally caught in strange magic net

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of its usual form, so the following letters are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the escapologist's name

explanation.surface: The great escapologist at last trapped in a weird magical net: how mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: The I joins the letters of 'magic net' before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic describes something puzzling and hard to interpret, a direct adjective synonym for mysterious.

clue.text: Popular Canadian dip is red-hot

parts.note: a dip in the ground or a downward slope

explanation.surface: A favourite Canadian sauce turns out to be fiery hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' looks like a sauce; it is a fall or slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incandescent glows with intense heat, so red-hot is a fair adjective match.

clue.text: Paste soon turns to mineral

indicators.note: turns as in changes form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wet paste quickly hardens into rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone, or steatite, is a soft talc-rich metamorphic rock used for carving.

clue.text: Cause of casualties in account given by police to hospital department?

explanation.surface: A police report handed to A&E about what put people in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the UK police detective branch; ENT is a hospital ear, nose and throat unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidents such as crashes and falls are a leading source of injured people needing treatment.

clue.text: Teacher of English taking old coin (gold)

parts.note: a gold coin once used across Europe

explanation.surface: An English master pockets an antique gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is anyone who instructs others professionally, a formal word for a teacher.

clue.text: Sort of sour-tasting liquid ruined diving career

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diver's career is soured and ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider vinegar is made by fermenting apple cider, giving an acidic liquid used in cooking and dressings.

clue.text: Ante up change for a kind of butter

indicators.note: a change of order is called for, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A poker player puts up his stake in exchange for a spread.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: peanut is the kind of butter, used attributively.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a spread of ground nuts, so the answer names a type of butter.

clue.text: Seeds coming from small openings in the skin

explanation.surface: Something growing out of little holes in your skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spores are the reproductive units of fungi and ferns, acting like seeds in flowering plants.

clue.text: Office holder, one new to money, secures university degree

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the money word wraps around the university and degree

parts.note: a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone newly in office with money to spare buys themselves a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a typical crossword degree; the coin word wraps round it with the university.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the person currently holding a particular post or official position.

clue.text: Man goes gathering fruit

indicators.note: gathering in means holding within, so the opening words hold the solution inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A man heads out to pick some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Sane people worried by a snoring problem

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Perfectly sane people kept anxious by a partner's snoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The A joins the fodder: ten letters of 'sane people' plus one make eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep apnoea is a medical disorder where breathing stops during sleep, and loud snoring is its classic symptom.

clue.text: Surviving son leaves navigational instrument

indicators.note: leaves in the sense of departs, so the son's letter goes out of the instrument

parts.note: used to measure angles of stars for navigation

explanation.surface: The only surviving son abandons his father's sextant.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence today, usually of documents or species, so it equals surviving.

clue.text: Chaplain boarding earlier ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and in, so the chaplain goes inside the other word

explanation.surface: The ship's chaplain came aboard ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts and fore-and-aft rigging.

clue.text: Fish, unusual British trout?

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their normal order

explanation.surface: An angler asks of an odd-looking catch whether it is some strange British trout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trout' tempts as the definition, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flatfish of European waters, prized as food.

clue.text: A boss set out to produce heat-resistant material

indicators.note: set out read as laid out afresh, so the preceding letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A manager sets out to make fireproof stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used for fireproofing and insulation.
